scope: The root complexity article directly links BPP, RP, ZPP, #P, Boolean circuits, circuit complexity, decision-tree complexity, communication complexity, and amortized analysis. These supply this section's immediate-link scope.
proof_status: Human-readable constructive reconstructions with primitive-recursive algorithms and finite numerical invariants. No claim of full object-iPRA derivation or Lean compilation.

sources.author: Leonard M. Adleman
sources.title: Two Theorems on Random Polynomial Time
sources.publication: 19th Annual Symposium on Foundations of Computer Science, pp. 75-83 (1978)
sources.access: Primary paper indexed by search; full open returned 502. Full finite proof is independently supplied; official-author Katz notes were also inspected.
sources.use: Historical source for random-polynomial-time nonuniform constructions; not a source for a formal iPRA claim.

sources.author: Clemens Lautemann
sources.title: BPP and the Polynomial Hierarchy
sources.access: Publisher abstract retrieved by search; direct open 403. The abstract explicitly identifies the counting proof of BPP inclusion at the second hierarchy level.
sources.use: Attribution of the theorem; report provides independent concrete integer parameters.

sources.author: Claude E. Shannon
sources.title: The Synthesis of Two-Terminal Switching Circuits
sources.access: Official Bell Labs publication record retrieved; CMU-hosted original PDF exceeded retrieval size limit.
sources.use: Historical circuit-counting attribution. The report's sixteen-gate-basis constants and bounded least-table algorithm are independently specified.

sources.author: Jonathan Katz
sources.title: Notes on Complexity Theory
sources.access: Full official instructor notes retrieved (129 pages).
sources.use: Standard randomized-class targets, BPP advice, and hierarchy inclusion. No source wording copied.

sources.author: Jonathan Katz
sources.title: Notes on Complexity Theory, Handout 5
sources.use: Confirms standard circuit upper-bound order and randomized definitions. Report's universal upper compiler uses a different residual-table construction with explicit constant 18, not the sharp Lupanov constant.

sources.author: Constantinos Daskalakis
sources.title: 6.006 Introduction to Algorithms, Lecture 10: Sorting
sources.use: Comparison-tree lower-bound target; report avoids the slides' use of Stirling's formula.

sources.author: Eric Blais
sources.title: Models of Computation, Chapter 21: Communication Complexity
sources.use: Shared leaf-output convention, fooling-set target, and exact n+1 deterministic equality bound.

validation.limits: Finite instance checks support implementation correctness; they do not prove the universally quantified statements.
